Senator Joe Baldacci testimony presenting
LD 1304 "RESOLUTION, Proposing an Amendment to the Constitution of Maine to Limit Property Tax Increases for Individuals 65 Years of Age or Older and Shift the Tax Burden to State Gaming Revenues."
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Taxation
May 1, 2025

Good morning Senator Grohoski, Representative Cloutier, and esteemed members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Taxation. My name is Joe Baldacci, and I represent Senate District 9, which includes Bangor and Hermon. I am pleased today to introduce LD 1304, "RESOLUTION, Proposing an Amendment to
the Constitution of Maine to Limit Property Tax Increases for Individuals 65 Years of Age or Older and Shift the Tax Burden to State Gaming Revenues."

The number one concern of hundreds of thousands of Maine homeowners is the escalating hikes in local
property taxes around the state.

In Bangor and around Maine, fairly aggressive property revaluations are underway and we, as
legislators, need to address those concerns. Why a tax cap for seniors? That is easy if we review some of
the important facts about our state:

1. The average age of the population is the oldest in the United States
2. Maine Seniors earning less than 55K per year -- 30% pay rent and a whopping 65%are I their

own homes.

3. 26% of all Maine seniors live alone, a relatively high percentage 4. In fact, Maine seniors are more likely to be widowed than in neighboring states like New

Hampshire or Vermont.

5. As of 2022, there were 312,000 seniors in Maine, an increase of 37.9% over the previous decade

6. An AARP survey recently found, unsurprisingly, that the overwhelming majority of seniors want to age in place in their own homes and communities. And that is generally a very positive thing.
7. According to national studies, the median household income of seniors who own their own home is $38,640 and the median home value in 2021 was 268K. A reasonable tax cap makes
sense.

10047135:
Testimony of the Maine Municipal Association
In Opposition to
LD 1304, RESOLUTION, Proposing an Amendment to the Constitution of Maine to Limit Property Tax Increases for Individuals 65 Years of Age or Older and Shift the Tax Burden to
State Gaming Revenues
May 1, 2025
Senator Grohoski, Representative Cloutier and members of the Taxation Committee, my name is Kate Dufour, and I am submitting testimony in opposition to LD 1304 on behalf of MMA's Legislative Policy Committee, which establishes the association's positions on all municipally relevant legislation.
While municipal leaders appreciate that the bill includes a self-funding mechanism to cover losses in property tax revenue, they oppose the use of age as an indicator for the ability to pay. The state's overreliance on the property tax to fund school, county, municipal and unfunded state mandates, places burdens on homeowners of all ages and incomes. If the Legislature is going to advance an amendment to Maine's constitution the resulting impact should deliver property tax relief to all homeowners. It might be argued that older residents have paid their fair share of taxes. However, when it comes to the assessment of property taxes, all homeowners should be treated similarly, as special treatment will lead to requests and pressures being placed on decisionmakers to extend exceptions to other property taxpayers.
Thank you for your time and consideration of the municipal perspective on this issue.
192222:
Testimony in Support of
LD I304: RESOLUTION, Proposing an Amendment to the Constitution of Maine to Limit
Property Tax Increases for Individuals 65 Years of Age or Older and Shift the Tax Burden to State Gaming Revenues
May 1, 2025
Chairpersons Senator Grohoski and Representative Cloutier and honorable members of the
Taxation Committee:
My name is Kerry Leichtman. I am a Certified Maine Assessor serving thejurisdictions of Camden and Rockport. I am testifying today in support of LD 1304.
LD 1304 offers a creative solution to paying for a limit of property taxes for seniors without
putting the burden on younger Mainers. I like the approach. I would pair this with a companion bill that offers relief to working families headed by permanent residences. That modification would offer a more generous tax fairness credit funded by sports betting revenues. This would not need to be a Constitutional amendment.
While I strongly support tax relief for seniors, we cannot pass over younger people who are
struggling to establish themselves in this increasingly expensive climate which is fueled by rising property values and property taxation.
Thank you for considering my testimony.

Sen. Grohoski, Rep. Cloutier, and members of the Taxation Committee, my name is Maura
Pillsburyand lam a tax policy analyst at Maine Center for Economic Policy. We are testifying in
opposition to LD 1304.
This bill proposes a constitutional amendment that would cap property tax increases at 2% per year for permanent Maine residents who are over 65 and have owned a home for at least 12 months. The bill requires the state to reimburse at least 90% of the cost to municipalities by creating an additional 2% tax on lottery tickets and sports betting.

We oppose legislation that provides a blanket property tax cap for older Mainers. Proposals like
this are not well targeted to help those who need it most. Wealthy older Mainers with higher property values will disproportionately benefit from this proposal. This is not a good use of
taxpayer dollars.
Further, we do not believe this measure belongs in the Constitution. If it is enacted as an
amendment, the Legislature could not easily change it if it becomes prohibitively expensive or no longer aligns with the State's needs. It would be unusual for a Constitutional amendment to stipulate a specific tax rate or a specific cap on taxes.

Currently, the Wabanaki tribes have sole authority to operate online sports betting in Maine, with 10% of proceeds going to the state. Our interpretation of this legislation is that the
Wa banaki Nations would be required to pay an additional 2% tax on their proceeds to the State. We oppose this.
Thank you for your time. I would be happy to answer any questions. maura@mecep.org
